Practice Glossary Comparisons

AIB-C01 concept comparisons

Side-by-side cues for similar exam ideas — terms link to the glossary. AWS exam guide · Nov 2026.

Unofficial AIB-C01 study sheet · duskyai.com/aib-c01/concepts/

Prompt engineering vs RAG vs fine-tuning

Prompt engineering

Fix format, tone, or constraints in the instructions — no new data or training.

RAG

Private or changing facts: fetch live docs at question time with citations.

Fine-tuning

Consistent style or task behavior that prompts alone cannot reach.

Rule Cheapest fix first: prompt → RAG → fine-tuning.

Quick check An internal FAQ bot quotes last month’s travel policy. What do you try first?

RAG over the live policy library — facts change often; fine-tuning on stale docs does not fix freshness.

AI vs ML vs generative AI

AI

Umbrella term for intelligent systems — not a specific technique.

ML

Predict, score, or classify from historical labeled data.

Generative AI

Create new text, images, audio, or code from a prompt.

Rule Predict from history = ML · create content = generative AI · fixed if-then = neither.

Quick check Predict which subscribers cancel next quarter from billing history?

Machine learning — scoring from patterns, not generating new content.

Rule-based automation vs AI

Rules

Fixed human-written logic — deterministic and auditable, never learns.

AI

Messy inputs or shifting patterns that no stable rule set can cover.

Rule Simple, stable, must reproduce exactly → rules. Varied or unstructured → AI.

Quick check Regulator sets exact numeric loan thresholds; auditors need 100% reproducible flags?

Rule-based automation — explicit thresholds and deterministic outcomes.

AWS Quick vs Bedrock vs SageMaker AI

AWS Quick

Business users with no builders — ready-made AI workspace (exam guide: Amazon Quick).

Bedrock

Developers shipping a generative app on foundation models, RAG, guardrails.

SageMaker AI

Custom train/deploy when off-the-shelf models will not fit.

Rule No engineers → Quick · dev building GenAI app → Bedrock · own model → SageMaker AI.

Quick check Finance team, no engineers, wants an assistant over spreadsheets this month?

AWS Quick — business users need a ready-made workspace, not a dev platform.

AI agent vs chatbot

Chatbot

Answers questions — no multi-step tool use.

AI agent

Plans steps, calls tools, checks results, acts or escalates.

Rule Actions across systems → agent · Q&A only → chatbot/assistant.

Quick check Tool must rebook a flight, file expenses, and email the manager?

AI agent — multi-step execution across systems, not just replies.

Augmentation vs automation

Augmentation

Human still delivers the outcome; AI drafts or recommends.

Automation

The system carries out the work end to end.

Rule Person still produces the result → augmentation. Per-case approval is HITL, not the same question.

Quick check AI drafts replies; reps edit and send themselves?

Augmentation — the human still sends the final message.

Token vs context window

Token

Billing unit for text in/out — cost rises with volume.

Context window

Cap on text considered in one request — tail content gets dropped.

Rule Bill shock → tokens · missing end of huge paste → context limit; fix with RAG chunks, not stuffing everything in.

Quick check 120-page lease drops clauses at the end with no error?

Context window exceeded — retrieve relevant sections instead of one giant prompt.

KPI vs ROI vs baseline

KPI

The metric the initiative exists to move.

ROI

(Benefits − TCO) ÷ cost — needs realized dollars, not minutes saved alone.

Baseline

Before measurement so you can credit AI for the delta.

Rule No before measure → no proven lift. Saved time ≠ ROI until tied to cost, capacity, or revenue.

Quick check 4-minute handle time after launch, but no pre-AI times recorded?

Missing baseline — cannot prove AI caused improvement.

Impact vs feasibility

Impact

Upside if the use case succeeds.

Feasibility

Data, skills, risk, and time to actually make it work.

Rule Pilot the case that wins on both. Huge impact + bad data → fix data first.

Quick check A: $5M upside, dirty data. B: $1M upside, ready data and owner?

B first — weak feasibility stalls A; run data readiness for A in parallel.

Build vs buy vs partner

Build

AI is the differentiator and you have in-house skills.

Buy

Common need, speed over customization.

Partner

Missing skills or deadline — vendor, integrator, or Marketplace.

Rule Differentiator + skills → build · commodity + deadline → buy/partner.

Quick check Standard invoice extraction in 60 days, no ML engineers?

Buy or partner — common capability and no team to build.

Consumption vs seat vs instance pricing

Consumption

Pay per token/API — pilots and spiky demand.

Seat-based

Predictable per-user fee for regular workspace use.

Instance / reserved

Steady high volume — Savings Plans when usage is proven.

Rule Unknown or variable usage → consumption. Do not reserve capacity before demand is stable.

Quick check 6-week pilot, unpredictable traffic — reserve capacity upfront?

No — start consumption-based; commit only when volume is steady.

Hallucination vs bias vs data-quality degradation

Hallucination

Confident facts or citations with no source.

Bias

Systematically worse outcomes for a group or segment.

Data-quality / drift

Worked at launch, accuracy decays as inputs shift.

Rule Invented detail → hallucination · one group always loses → bias · slow decay after go-live → drift.

Quick check Forecasts miss after new product lines and broken warehouse feeds?

Data-quality degradation / drift — distribution shifted, model code did not.

Guardrails vs oversight vs governance

Guardrails

Automated block/filter on unsafe I/O in real time.

Oversight

People approve (HITL) or monitor/override (HOTL).

Governance

Policies, inventory, approval gates, owners.

Rule Auto block → guardrail · person signs off → oversight · who owns risk org-wide → governance.

Quick check Three chatbots, three privacy rules, one prompt filter added — still broken?

Governance layer — shared policy, inventory, owners per use case.

HITL vs HOTL

HITL

Human approves before each decision ships.

HOTL

System acts; humans monitor and can reverse.

Rule Must not act without sign-off → HITL · auto-block with analyst override → HOTL.

Quick check Fraud AI blocks cards; analysts reverse false positives?

Human-on-the-loop — automated action, human monitoring.

Explainability vs transparency

Explainability

Why this specific output or decision happened.

Transparency

Disclose that AI is involved and its limits.

Rule “Why was I declined?” → explainability · “You’re chatting with AI” → transparency.

Quick check Bank must list factors behind a credit rejection?

Explainability — reason for that decision.

ISO 22989 vs 23053 vs 42001

22989

AI vocabulary — not a cert.

23053

ML system framework — not a cert.

42001

Certifiable org AI management system — vendor cert ≠ your workflows certified.

Rule Vendor 42001 certifies the vendor’s management system, not your deployment.

Quick check Vendor says their 42001 means your workflow is certified?

False — your org still owns governance of how you use AI.

PoC vs pilot vs scale

PoC

Time-boxed feasibility — can it work at all?

Pilot

Real users/data with measured outcomes.

Scale

Production owner, monitoring, support, routines.

Rule Demo ≠ production. Many stuck pilots = pilot purgatory — missing owner and ops.

Quick check Five great demos last year, none in daily ops, no monitoring owner?

Failed at scale — run-state ownership never built.

Owner vs CoE

Accountable owner

Answers for one system’s outcomes and risks.

AI CoE

Standards, patterns, enablement — not owning every delivery.

Rule Who is blamed for failure → owner. Who helps all teams → CoE (must not become the only build shop).

Quick check Central team builds every BU model — 9-month backlog?

CoE as bottleneck — enable BUs; owners stay accountable.

Literacy vs upskilling vs change

AI literacy

Baseline skill to use and question AI in role.

Upskilling

Training programs to close skill gaps.

Change management

Incentives, workflows, leadership so behavior shifts.

Rule Trained but still old process → change management, not more courses.

Quick check Dispatchers trained on optimizer; bonuses reward manual routes?

Change management — fix incentives and workflow, not training alone.

Risk classification

EU AI Act tiers

  1. 1 · Prohibited

    Banned

    Social scoring, manipulative exploitation.

  2. 2 · High

    High risk

    Hiring, credit — documentation, oversight, conformity.

  3. 3 · Limited

    Limited

    Disclose AI chatbots and synthetic content.

  4. 4 · Minimal

    Minimal

    Spam filters, basic recommendations — no extra AI Act duties.

Rule Classify the use case first; reclassify if purpose, audience, or data changes.

Heuristics

Six decision rules

  1. 01

    Smallest change first

    Try prompt engineering before RAG, and RAG before fine-tuning or custom training.

  2. 02

    Measure before and after

    Capture a baseline or run a controlled A/B comparison before claiming ROI or savings.

  3. 03

    Owner before scale

    Pair every production rollout with a named accountable owner and run-state operations so pilots do not stall.

  4. 04

    Enable rather than only ban

    Shadow AI persists when staff have a real need and no approved option; pair clear rules with sanctioned tools.

  5. 05

    Human review scales with harm

    Use human-in-the-loop approval for high-harm or irreversible decisions, and human-on-the-loop or confidence escalation for lower-risk flows.

  6. 06

    Data readiness gates the pilot

    High business value paired with broken or missing data is a data-quality project first, not a quick pilot.
